The test image shows a severely stunted corn plant with dried, brown/dead leaves, much shorter than surrounding healthy green plants. This is a whole_plant presentation.

Top candidates from whole_plant classes: Corn_Stunt_Spiroplasma, Stewart_S_Disease, Maize_Chlorotic_Dwarf_Virus, Crazy_Top, Bacterial_Stalk_Rot, Anthracnose_Leaf_Spot_And_Top_Dieback, Goss_S_Wilt, Maize_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus.

Let me view one reference from each top candidate.
Stewart's Disease reference shows a wilted, collapsed plant with dried brown leaves among healthy corn, quite similar to the test image. Let me check other candidates.
Corn Stunt shows reddish/pink discoloration on leaves, not matching the test image. Let me continue checking.
Bacterial Stalk Rot shows taller plants, not matching the severely stunted seedling. Let me check more.
Crazy Top shows bushy green leaf proliferation, very different from the test image. Not a match.
MCDV shows stunted but still green plants with yellowing. Not matching the severely dried test image.
MDMV shows mosaic/streaking patterns on green leaves. Not matching.
Goss's Wilt shows leaf lesions with freckles, not whole plant death. Not matching.

I've now viewed 8 reference images across 8 different classes. The strongest visual match is clearly **Stewart's Disease** (view 1), which showed a wilted, dried, collapsed young corn plant surrounded by healthy green corn, nearly identical to the test image.

The test image shows:
- A severely stunted/wilted corn plant with completely dried brown leaves
- Plant appears to be in the seedling wilt phase
- Surrounded by healthy, tall green corn plants
- Single affected plant (scattered pattern)

This matches Stewart's Disease seedling wilt phase: seedlings wilt and die, with bleached/dried leaves. The reference image was a close visual match.

Other candidates were ruled out: Corn Stunt (reddish leaves, not seen), Crazy Top (bushy green proliferation), MCDV/MDMV (still green with mosaic/yellowing), Bacterial Stalk Rot (taller plants), Goss's Wilt (leaf lesions, not whole plant death).
